title: Least-Privilege IAM module with OPA policy bundles and GitOps upgrade path
creator: Aria Patel
description: Create a Terraform module that generates least-privilege IAM/RBAC scaffolding for Private (VPC) deployments while producing versioned OPA policy bundles and a safe GitOps upgrade path. The module should support: 1) opinionated defaults for service account and role templates, 2) permission boundaries and conditional IAM Conditions for network-scoped principals, 3) optional automated bundle build (local container or CI builder) that outputs an OPA bundle artifact (S3/GCS/OCI), and 4) a GitOps-friendly upgrade flow that can be validated and rolled back. Deliver a playbook for upgrades, health checks for permission drift, and CT/CI hooks that validate generated policies against a set of eval prompts and sample workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module inputs/outputs documented and stable in README; consumers can supply principal prefixes, resource name prefixes, and explicit allow-lists.
Module produces reusable IAM artifacts: aws_iam_policy (or cloud equivalent), permission boundaries, and role templates with clearly scoped inline policies.
Build pipeline produces an OPA policy bundle artifact (tar.gz/oci) with semantic version tags and checksum metadata stored alongside the module outputs.
A documented GitOps upgrade flow exists: new policy bundle commit -> CI validation (dry-run admission tests + static lint) -> promotion to canary -> automatic fallback on regression within X hours.
Health checks detect drift: automated weekly job lists policy differences vs. deployed roles and flags items for review in Console and Slack channel.
Security review completed and approved (security_review_required flag true) and module passes basic fuzz tests in CI (no wildcard actions by default).
implementation_notes: Module API: inputs include environment (prod/stage), service_account_prefix, additional_principals (list), allowed_actions (list), network_condition_map (json string), kms_key_arn for secrets, opa_bundle_destination (s3:// or oci://), and enable_permission_boundaries (bool string).

Internals: use terraform templatefile + jsonencode to generate IAM policy documents; create aws_iam_policy + aws_iam_policy_attachment resources and aws_iam_role with assume_role_policy built from principals input.
Versioning: use aws_iam_policy_version to stage new versions and keep last N versions; output opa_bundle_version and bundle_checksum as module outputs.

OPA bundle pipeline: provide a helper Dockerfile and CI job that pulls generated JSON policies, compiles them into a rego bundle, signs metadata, and pushes to configured artifact registry; module exposes data source for the bundle path.

GitOps upgrade: recommend controller pattern (e.g., flux/argocd or internal agent) that observes a bundle image/tar path; CI runs admission-controller dry-run tests against a lightweight k8s cluster with test manifests.
Permission boundaries: attach permission boundary policies to created roles; boundary templates include network-scoped conditions (ipV4/CIDR) and resource tags to prevent cross-customer access.
Backward compatibility: provide a migration helper script (terraform state mv patterns and role import examples) and mark any breaking inputs clearly in docs.
Observability: emit CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics for bundle deploys and a tagging convention (infra:priv-iam-module, module_version:<v>) to surface health in Console.
Cross-cloud note: abstract policy creation via provider-specific helpers but keep OPA bundle format cloud-agnostic (policy inputs include provider and resource type mapping).
risks: Privilege creep if consumers bypass allowed_actions; mitigate by default-deny and CI linting with explicit allow lists.
Rollout regressions could take down control-plane paths; require canary gates and automatic rollback thresholds in playbook.
Stateful upgrades: policy updates may require role re-attachments; document maintenance windows and provide zero-downtime attachment steps.
Secret handling for bundle signing: must integrate with customer KMS/HSM and avoid committing private keys to repo.
Cross-account assumptions: improper trust policies could escalate privileges; include strict tests and use permission boundaries by default.
test_plan: Unit: terraform plan for example configs (prod/stage) with sample principals, assert no wildcard actions produced.
Integration: CI job builds OPA bundle, runs rego tests, and performs dry-run admission against staging cluster with seeded resources.
Canary: deploy bundle to a low-impact namespace, run synthetic traffic, monitor metrics and error rates for 24h before promoting.
Drift detection: weekly job compares generated policy JSON vs live IAM roles/policies and opens issues for manual review.
Rollback exercises: simulate a failed rollout and validate rollback steps in playbook (time to recovery target defined).
